summary: Clarify and formalize ephemeral prod-log access workflow for minimized customer payload slices
description:
Issue summary: Request from SRE and SOC to standardize the approval and provisioning workflow when engineers need timeboxed, minimized extracts of production inference logs for compliance/security investigations. The current ad-hoc process leads to inconsistent redaction, unclear TTLs for access tokens, and no consistent audit breadcrumb for legal reviewers.

Context: Multiple recent internal requests relied on informal Slack approvals and manual redaction steps. Compliance asked for a deterministic checklist that engineers and on-call can follow without blocking investigations, while preserving data minimization and auditable controls.
impact: Unclear workflows increase time-to-resolution for security/compliance investigations and raise the risk of excessive data exposure. Non-deterministic redaction and token lifetimes complicate legal audit and SOC reviews.
environment: prod | us-east-1 (primary logs), supporting cross-region slices as needed
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Engineer asks for a 'sample of requests' from prod inference logs to reproduce an error; requests sent to #support with no formal approval ticket.
2) SRE pulls raw traces and performs ad-hoc redaction locally (mix of regex and manual edits).
3) Engineer receives zipped traces via shared drive with no clear TTL or audit link.
4) Legal later requests provenance and the redaction rationale; SRE cannot produce a single, auditable approval trail.
logs: Sample log pull command referenced: gsutil cp gs://redwood-prod-logs/inference/2026-03-09/segment-42.jsonl ./
Example trace id: trace-3f2a7c (redacted copy attached in private compliance bundle)
SRE extraction note: 'masked_user_id: <sha256>' applied via local script mask_payloads_v2.sh
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11: Interviewed SRE oncall (Jonas Miller) — current practice is to default to maximal redaction then add context on request. No TTL enforcement in shared drive.
2026-03-12: Legal (Priya Sharma) requires: 1) justification, 2) minimal slice, 3) cryptographic hashing of IDs, 4) audit trail with approver identity.
Observed gaps: no standardized redaction patterns for token-like substrings; no automated hashing salt provenance; manual storage uses team drives without automated expunge.
comments: Aisha Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Filed after SOC escalated an ambiguous extraction in INC-20260309. Requesting a formal workflow and a checklist template.

Connor Liu (Assignee) 2026-03-11: Proposed owning the workflow doc and implementing a short-lived presigned storage mechanism (S3 pre-signed URL with automatic deletion). Will prototype policy and checklist.

Priya Sharma (Legal) 2026-03-12: Legal input: approve only minimized slices with explicit justification. Require records retained in audit log for 7 years for certain regulated customers; need per-request metadata and approver identity.
Jonas Miller (SRE) 2026-03-12: Note — we should integrate with 'privileged-access' RBAC and generate a ticketed signed-off artifact that ties to the change.
resolution: Work-in-progress: Agreed on a 3-step formal workflow and technical guardrails. Action items completed in this ticket: 1) Drafted 'Ephemeral Prod Log Access Checklist' and placed in Confluence, 2) Implemented prototype S3 presigned URL workflow with 24-hour TTL + server-side delete job, 3) Added standard redaction script (mask_payloads_v3) to infra-tools with deterministic salt stored in KMS access logs. Remaining: roll out RBAC self-serve button in internal Console and automate audit event linking to Jira ticket.
